newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Eastern offers 140 mln H-shrs in HK IPO.
newsitem.headline: China Eastern offers 140 mln H-shrs in HK IPO.

text.p: China Eastern Airlines Corp Ltd said on Monday it is offering 140 million H-shares, representing 10 percent of a global offering of 1.4 billion shares, in Hong Kong at a price ranging from HK$1.22 to HK$1.38 per share.
H-shares are Hong Kong-listed shares of China-incorporated enterprises.
China Eastern Airlines said it plans to raise a total of up to about HK$1.9 billion in gross proceeds from the global offering of 1.4 billion shares.
The global offering includes three tranches -- the Hong Kong public offering representing 10 percent of the total, and the U.S. and international offerings representing 45 percent each.
The proportion of the Hong Kong offering will increase to a maximum of 30 percent of the total global offering if the Hong Kong tranche is oversubscribed by 10 times or more.
Based on an offering price of HK$1.22 to HK$1.38 per H-share, the company's market capitalisation will be HK$1.71 billion to HK$1.93 billion, the offering's prospectus said.
The offering price represents a prospective price/earnings multiple of 9.4 times to 10.6 times on a fully diluted basis, and 7.2 times to 8.1 times on a weighted average basis.
The airline said it estimates consolidated profit after tax and minority interest but before extraordinaries of not less than 550 million yuan for the year ended December 31, 1996.
The global offering will initally represent 31.8 percent of the issued share capital of the company, and 34.9 percent if an overallotment option is exercised in full.

The company has granted U.S. underwriters an overallotment option of up to 2.1 million additional American Depository Shares (ADS) or 210 million H-shares to cover overalloments in the U.S. or international offerings.
The Hong Kong IPO will run from January 28-31, with the final share price expected to be fixed on January 31.
Trading in the ADS on the New York Stock Exchange is scheduled to begin on February 4. Dealing in H-shares on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange is scheduled to commence on February 5.
About 60 percent of the net proceeds of the combined offering will be used to acquire new aircraft and related spare parts and equipment.
The company said it has entered into contracts to buy nine McDonnell Douglas MD-90 aircraft and five Airbus Industrie A340 aircraft to be delivered between 1997 and 2000.
About six percent of the proceeds will be used to buy an Airbus A300-600R flight simulator.

The balance will be put towards financing all or part of the estimated capital expenditure to be incured in 1997 for the construction of airport facilities at the new Pudong airport and additional maintenance facilities in Shanghai.

China Eastern airlines operates 114 routes, 91 of them domestic. It makes more than 1,100 scheduled flights a week from 44 airports in China and abroad, including 100 international flights per week, serving 13 cities in eight countries.
The company has a fleet of 64 aircraft including 41 jet passenger planes and one jet cargo plane.
Morgan Stanley Asia Ltd is the global coordinator of the share issue, with ABN Amro Rothschild as the co-sponsor.
